test.title: Evaluate yourself
test.eyebrow: Test · real timers, no going back
q.noBack: No back button in Test mode — just like MEPS.
q.timeout: Time is up — unanswered items count as wrong.
test.diagDesc: 5 questions from every subtest at the official pace — about {min} minutes. Produces your first AFQT estimate and weak-area ranking.
test.fullDesc: All 10 subtests, 135 scored questions, official time limits, adaptive difficulty, no back button.
test.singleDesc: One subtest under its official clock. Good for pacing drills on the fast sections (WK, EI, GS).
test.tryoutNote: On the real test, tryout (unscored) questions may add up to 15 items and extra time to any subtest. This app uses scored items only.
test.beginNote: When you press Begin the official clock starts.
test.rule.answerAll: Answer every question. A wrong guess costs nothing, and a blank counts as wrong and can cost you slightly more.
test.rule.keepMoving: Do not stall on one question. A run of wrong or blank answers at the end of a subtest costs extra, so keep moving and finish.
test.rule.harder: Harder questions are a good sign. The test only steps up after you get one right.
test.rule.noBack: You cannot go back. Once you submit an answer that question is closed, exactly like the real CAT-ASVAB.
test.rule.noCalc: No calculator. Use scratch paper and a pencil, the only tools you get at MEPS.
test.rule.restart: If you leave in the middle of a subtest, that subtest starts over from the beginning.
test.breakNote: Take a breath. Next up: {next}. The clock only starts when you press Begin.

results.title: Score simulator
results.formula: AFQT = 2·VE + AR + MK, where VE comes from WK + PC. Estimates from the adaptive approximation — treat as ±5 points.
results.meets: Meets the {branch} minimum ({min}) for high-school graduates.
results.below: Below the {branch} minimum ({min}) for high-school graduates — the weak-area list shows where to gain.
results.noComposites: No named composites for this branch yet — ratings use per-job sums.
results.linesNote: Branch minimums change with recruiting needs. Last checked {date} — confirm with your recruiter.
results.weak: Where to spend your next hour
results.weakNote: Ranked by gap × AFQT leverage, not by raw score.
results.none: Nothing yet — take a test or practice first.
results.timingNote: Red = over the official per-item budget. ✕ = items left unanswered at time-out, the case the real CAT penalizes.
results.reviewNote: Every miss links to the trick that would have saved it.
learn.title: Lessons by topic
plan.title: Study plan
plan.note: Subtests are ordered by how much they hold your AFQT back. Inside each one: topics you missed, then shaky ones, then topics the app has not tested yet (★ = how often they appear on the real test). The map sharpens with every question you practice.
home.firstStep: Start with the Diagnostic: 5 questions from every subtest at the official pace.
home.welcomeIntro: This app takes you from “where am I” to “ready for MEPS”. Everything is saved on this device and works offline. Four areas: Learn (lessons), Practice (untimed drills with explanations), Test (real timers, no going back), Results (your AFQT estimate and study plan).
home.w1d: Pick your branch and a target AFQT in Settings (the gear, top right).
home.w2d: About 70 minutes, 50 questions, official pace. It finds your strong and weak subtests.
home.w3d: Results shows what you missed, what is shaky and what is not tested yet — each with a lesson and a drill.
home.w4d: Work the plan, then take a full test. The app never repeats a question while it has new ones.
home.welcomeInstall: Tip: on your phone, use the browser’s “Add to Home Screen” to install the app and use it offline.
results.needAll: The AFQT needs a timed score in AR, WK, PC and MK.
